1 What are we doing?

A small local web application whose browser-facing web service fetches and displays a fixed item list from a separate HTTP API.

Target
local · local machine · project alias demo-app
Components (2)
api — Serves health and item-list JSON endpoints on local port 18081
web — Serves the browser page and checks the web-to-API chain on local port 18080
Deployment shape
Run api.mjs and web.mjs as detached local Node.js processes bound to 127.0.0.1. The browser opens web on port 18080; web calls the API on port 18081. Neither service is exposed beyond this machine.

3 Why this plan?
Why this shape
The application has no dependencies or persistent data and already includes a runner that starts, checks, and stops both processes. Two local Node.js processes are the smallest sufficient shape.
Heavier options not needed
Docker Compose — The local Node.js runtime is compatible and the provided runner needs no dependency installation or container layer.
Orchestration cluster — A two-process single-user demo does not need scheduling, autoscaling, or multi-host recovery.
Managed database — The API serves a fixed in-memory list and stores no data.
Load balancer — The app is for browser use on this machine only and has one web process.
Assumptions
The app is intended for local use from a browser on this machine, not for public network access.
The default ports 18080 and 18081 remain available when the services are started.

Run node run.mjs down from the demo-app workspace; it stops the recorded PIDs and checks that ports 18080 and 18081 are free.
Known to be unverified
No public or external network access was requested or verified; the app is intentionally bound to 127.0.0.1.
Automated visual inspection of the system browser was unavailable; the exact browser URL was opened and its HTTP HTML content was independently verified.
Fragile
The app uses detached local processes rather than a system service, so a reboot or manual process termination will stop it; node run.mjs status detects this.
Ports 18080 and 18081 must remain available; conflicts are reported by node run.mjs up or status.
